_disclaimer: Illustrative FIXTURE templates for the chinese-herbal-oncology-support proposal. None are patient-visible until an oncology-dietitian approval (matching the same immutable version) is recorded. No template includes an automatic individualized calorie/protein calculator, a cancer-specific diet, or a herbal soup/medicated congee/concentrated tea/mushroom/ginseng/astragalus/licorice/formula-sachet item presented as ordinary food -- any such item is explicitly routed to the herb/supplement safety workflow in knowledge/chinese-herbal-oncology/example_evidence_cards.json instead.
not_a_cure_statement: Nutrition support in every template below exists to support strength, energy, and treatment tolerance. It is not a cancer cure and does not control tumor growth.
cancer_specific_diet_policy: No cancer-type-specific diet is included because no current oncology guideline was identified in this pass supporting a distinct diet for any exact disease/treatment context. If such evidence is identified in a future pass, it will be added as its own guideline-cited template, never inferred from survey or traditional-use material.

templates.goal: Support adequate energy and protein intake despite reduced appetite, early satiety, or unintentional weight loss.
templates.intended_population: Adults with cancer experiencing reduced appetite, early satiety, or unintentional weight loss during or after treatment.
may_apply_when: reduced appetite during or after treatment
unintentional weight loss not yet under separate dietitian workup
unsuitable_when: dysphagia/aspiration risk (use the mucositis/swallowing template and refer for swallow assessment instead)
rapid unintentional weight loss already under active dietitian/medical workup -- defer to that individualized plan
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Small, frequent, energy- and protein-dense meals/snacks rather than three large meals; fortify usual foods rather than restricting food groups; separate fluids from meals if early fullness is prominent.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Congee cooked with extra egg or minced meat/fish stirred in for protein
Steamed egg custard (egg, water or stock)
Soft tofu with minced meat or fish
Small portions of soft-cooked noodles with broth
Rice porridge with soft-cooked vegetables and a protein source
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Some traditional Chinese dietary-therapy frameworks describe reduced appetite as a sign of weakened Pi-Wei (spleen-stomach) function and favor warm, well-cooked, easily digested food. This is presented as cultural/traditional context only, not as biomedical rationale for why these foods might help.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Small energy- and protein-dense meals reduce the volume needed per sitting while meeting intake targets; standard oncology-nutrition guidance, not specific to any herb or tradition.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Prioritize protein and energy density per meal; texture soft/moist if chewing or swallowing is also affected; no automatic individualized calorie/protein calculation -- an oncology dietitian sets individual targets.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: Do not add medicinal congee, herbal soups, concentrated teas, ginseng, Astragalus, or formula sachets to 'help appetite' -- any such addition is a herb/supplement decision requiring the interaction workflow in example_evidence_cards.json, not a food choice.

cautions.diabetes: Fortifying with simple sugars/sweetened supplements needs glycemic-aware substitution.
cautions.hepatic: Individualize protein fortification with hepatic impairment.
cautions.cardiac: Fluid/sodium load from fortified soups or broths needs cardiac-aware individualization.
cautions.dysphagia: Use the mucositis/swallowing template instead if present.
cautions.ostomy: Individualize fiber/fat content with an ostomy nurse/dietitian.
cautions.obstruction: Not appropriate if obstruction is suspected.
cautions.allergy: Screen all substitutions (egg, soy/tofu, fish) for known allergy.
cautions.immunosuppression: Apply the neutropenia/food-safety template's preparation rules concurrently if applicable.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: weight loss greater than roughly 5% of body weight in a month
inability to keep food or fluids down
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Maintain fluid and food intake while nausea/vomiting is managed by prescribed antiemetics.
templates.intended_population: Adults with treatment-related nausea/vomiting, antiemetics already prescribed or being arranged.
may_apply_when: treatment-related nausea with antiemetics prescribed or in progress
unsuitable_when: vomiting preventing any fluid retention -- needs urgent clinical contact, not a diet template
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Bland, room-temperature or cool, low-aroma foods; small frequent sips of fluid; avoid very fatty, very sweet, or strongly spiced foods if they worsen symptoms; eat before feeling very hungry.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Plain congee
Plain steamed rice with a small amount of soft protein
Plain soft tofu
Clear, mild broth-based soup without heavy spice or strong aroma
Plain steamed bun (mantou) in small pieces
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Warm, plain, easily digested food is traditionally favored for digestive discomfort in Chinese food-therapy frameworks. Cultural/traditional context only, not a claim that this treats chemotherapy-induced nausea.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Small, frequent, bland, low-aroma intake reduces gastric distension and aroma triggers; standard oncology supportive-care nutrition principle.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Prioritize fluid/electrolyte retention first, then energy, then protein as tolerated; texture soft and plain.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: Ordinary culinary ginger (e.g. a few thin slices in tea) is a food/tolerance question, not an antiemetic substitute -- see card-culinary-ginger-nonequivalence. A concentrated ginger product must never replace prescribed antiemetics and needs pharmacist review.

cautions.diabetes: Watch simple-sugar content of any tolerated sweet/bland fluids.
cautions.hepatic: Not specifically restrictive beyond general tolerance.
cautions.cardiac: Large-volume fluid replacement needs cardiac-aware pacing.
cautions.dysphagia: Combine with the mucositis/swallowing template if present.
cautions.ostomy: Individualize fluid/fiber choices with the ostomy team.
cautions.obstruction: Not appropriate if obstruction is suspected.
cautions.immunosuppression: Apply neutropenia food-safety rules concurrently if applicable.

templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Maintain safe intake when the mouth/throat is sore, dry, or chewing/swallowing is effortful or painful.
templates.intended_population: Adults with diagnosed oral mucositis, treatment-related dry mouth, or mild chewing/swallowing difficulty already assessed as not an aspiration risk.
may_apply_when: mild chewing/swallowing difficulty assessed as low aspiration risk
unsuitable_when: any suspected aspiration risk or diagnosed dysphagia requiring a speech-and-swallow therapist's texture plan -- defer entirely to that plan
acute severe mucositis unable to swallow saliva
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Soft, moist, lukewarm-to-cool foods; avoid acidic, very salty, very spicy, coarse, or crusty textures; moisten dry foods with sauces, broths, or soft tofu; small bites.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Well-cooked, soft congee
Steamed egg custard
Soft tofu, plain or in a mild broth
Mashed soft-cooked vegetables
Soft, well-cooked noodles in mild broth
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Cooling, moist, plain preparations are traditionally favored for irritated tissue in some Chinese dietary-therapy frameworks. Cultural/traditional context only, not treatment for mucositis.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Soft, moist, non-irritant textures reduce mechanical/chemical irritation of inflamed oral/esophageal mucosa; standard supportive-care nutrition principle.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Texture is the primary lever here; protein/energy density secondary but still prioritized within tolerance; avoid extreme temperatures.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: Preliminary oral turmeric/curcumin findings for mucositis (see card-culinary-turmeric-curcumin-nonequivalence) are a distinct, formulation-uncertain supportive-care research question, not a validated food or supplement recommendation, and must not be added here without oncology-dietitian and pharmacy review.

cautions.diabetes: As above for any sweetened soft foods.
cautions.hepatic: No specific restriction beyond general tolerance.
cautions.dysphagia: This template excludes diagnosed dysphagia -- defer to speech-and-swallow plan.
cautions.obstruction: Not applicable to oral/pharyngeal mucositis specifically, but screen if concurrent GI symptoms exist.
cautions.immunosuppression: Apply neutropenia food-safety rules concurrently if applicable.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: coughing or choking with food/fluids (possible aspiration)
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Reduce stool frequency/fluidity while maintaining hydration and electrolyte intake.
templates.intended_population: Adults with treatment-related diarrhea without fever or blood in stool.
may_apply_when: treatment-related diarrhea without fever or blood in stool
unsuitable_when: fever, blood in stool, or signs of infection (contact clinical team, do not manage with diet alone)
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Temporarily lower-insoluble-fiber, lower-fat, lower-lactose pattern; frequent small sips of fluid/electrolyte replacement; reintroduce fiber gradually as symptoms settle.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Plain congee or rice-based porridge without heavy legumes
Plain steamed rice
Well-cooked, peeled soft vegetables
Clear broth with a pinch of salt for electrolyte support
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Plain rice congee is a traditional household approach to loose stools in many Chinese communities. Cultural/traditional note only, not a validated antidiarrheal treatment.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Temporary reduction of insoluble fiber and fat, plus oral fluid/electrolyte replacement, is standard supportive management pending medical review if diarrhea persists.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Fluid/electrolyte replacement first priority; reintroduce protein/energy sources as tolerated once stool frequency improves.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: No herbal antidiarrheal (e.g. concentrated formula sachets) is included or implied; any such product requires the herb/supplement safety workflow.

cautions.hepatic: No specific restriction beyond general tolerance.
cautions.dysphagia: Combine with the mucositis/swallowing template if present.
cautions.ostomy: High-output ostomy needs its own specialist fluid/electrolyte plan, not this general template alone.
cautions.obstruction: Not applicable to diarrhea specifically but screen if mixed bowel symptoms exist.
cautions.immunosuppression: Fever plus diarrhea during known/suspected neutropenia is a medical emergency, not a diet question.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: known or suspected neutropenia with fever (medical emergency)
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Support comfortable, regular bowel movements while explicitly screening out obstruction/impaction before any fiber/fluid advice is applied.
templates.intended_population: Adults with mild treatment- or opioid-related constipation with no obstruction/impaction red flags present.
may_apply_when: mild treatment- or opioid-related constipation with no red flags below present
unsuitable_when: any red flag below is present -- this template must not be shown or followed if so
known bowel surgery/stoma without surgical-team clearance for dietary fiber changes
obstruction_and_impaction_red_flags_scre: no bowel movement or gas passage for several days with worsening pain
suspected fecal impaction (e.g. overflow diarrhea around a hard mass)
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Gradual increase in fluids and soluble fiber if no red flags are present; regular meal timing; light activity as tolerated.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Well-hydrated soft fruit such as pear or papaya
Warm water first thing in the morning
Soft-cooked leafy greens
Congee with added soft vegetables
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Warm water and well-cooked, moist foods are traditionally favored for regularity in some Chinese dietary-therapy frameworks. This explicitly excludes any laxative herb, purgative formula, or cleansing regimen, which are out of scope for this module.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Gradual fiber and fluid increase is standard first-line dietary management for uncomplicated constipation once obstruction/impaction has been excluded.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Fluid increase paced to cardiac/renal tolerance; fiber increased gradually to avoid bloating.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: No herbal laxative, purgative formulation, or supplement is included or implied.

cautions.hepatic: No specific restriction beyond general tolerance.
cautions.ostomy: Individualize fiber changes with the ostomy team.
cautions.obstruction: This template is explicitly unsuitable if obstruction/impaction is suspected -- screen first.
cautions.immunosuppression: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: any obstruction/impaction red flag listed above
no improvement after a few days of the flexible pattern
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Maintain adequate intake when taste or smell changes make usual foods unpalatable.
templates.intended_population: Adults with treatment-related taste/smell alteration (dysgeusia/anosmia-type changes).
may_apply_when: treatment-related taste or smell changes affecting intake
unsuitable_when: concurrent mucositis/dysphagia -- combine with those templates rather than using this one alone
concurrent nausea -- combine with the nausea template
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Trial-and-adjust approach: some patients tolerate stronger flavors better, others need blander food; serve food at room temperature or cool if hot food's aroma is aversive; rinse mouth before eating if helpful; use non-metal utensils if metallic taste is reported.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Congee with a mild, patient-preferred flavor adjustment (more or less seasoning as tolerated)
Cold or room-temperature tofu dishes if hot food aroma is aversive
Soft fruit for a refreshing, non-metallic-tasting option
Clear broths if stronger-flavored soups are aversive
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Not applicable as a distinct traditional item here -- this template is symptom-driven rather than tradition-driven; any traditional flavor-balancing concept (e.g. the five-flavors framework) may be mentioned only as cultural context for why a food is chosen, never as the reason it is expected to help the underlying symptom.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Taste/smell alteration is a recognized, usually temporary treatment side effect; individualized trial-and-adjust flavor/temperature strategies are standard supportive-care nutrition practice.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Prioritize whatever food form the patient can tolerate to meet protein/energy needs; texture and temperature are the primary levers, not a fixed menu.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: Do not add a concentrated spice/herb product to 'restore taste' -- any such product is a herb/supplement decision requiring the interaction workflow, not a food choice. Ordinary culinary spices used only as flavoring, if tolerated, are not described as therapeutic per this module's spice-handling rule.

cautions.diabetes: Flavor adjustments using sugar need glycemic-aware substitution.
cautions.renal: Salt-based flavor adjustments need renal-function-aware limits.
cautions.hepatic: No specific restriction beyond general tolerance.
cautions.cardiac: Salt-based flavor adjustments need cardiac-aware limits.
cautions.dysphagia: Combine with the mucositis/swallowing template if present.
cautions.ostomy: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.
cautions.allergy: Screen any new flavoring ingredient for allergy.
cautions.immunosuppression: Apply neutropenia food-safety rules concurrently if applicable.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: intake inadequate to maintain weight/hydration despite trial-and-adjust strategies -- refer to oncology dietitian for individualized plan
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Reduce foodborne-illness risk during neutropenia, stem-cell transplantation, or substantial immunosuppression.
templates.intended_population: Adults with clinician-confirmed neutropenia, stem-cell transplant recipients, or others with substantial immunosuppression.
may_apply_when: clinician-confirmed neutropenia, transplant, or significant immunosuppression
unsuitable_when: not currently neutropenic/immunosuppressed -- do not apply unnecessarily restrictive food-safety rules outside this window
templates.flexible_food_pattern: Well-cooked foods only; avoid unpasteurized dairy and juice, raw or undercooked meat/egg/fish, raw sprouts, unwashed raw produce, and buffet/leftover food held at room temperature; wash hands and produce thoroughly; use safe water.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: Well-cooked congee and vegetables instead of raw salads
Pasteurized soy milk/dairy instead of unpasteurized
Freshly boiled and cooled water or well-boiled soups instead of raw juices
Fully cooked tofu and egg dishes instead of raw or lightly cooked preparations
Fully cooked noodle/rice dishes instead of raw sprout-topped dishes
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: Not applicable as a distinct traditional item -- this template is safety-driven; any traditional raw-food, raw-juice, or lightly-preserved practice is explicitly set aside during neutropenia/transplant/immunosuppression regardless of tradition.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Neutropenic and transplant/immunosuppressed patients have materially higher risk of severe infection from foodborne pathogens; raw sprouts, unpasteurized products, and undercooked animal products are established higher-risk items in oncology food-safety guidance.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: Food-safety preparation rules take priority; protein/energy needs are met through well-cooked equivalents of usual foods, not through restriction of food groups.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: No raw herbal juice, concentrated tea, or unprocessed mushroom product is recommended during this period; medicinal mushrooms in particular (see card-ganoderma-mixed-cancers, card-psk-resected-gi-cancer) carry their own separate safety review and are never treated as an ordinary food during immunosuppression.

cautions.diabetes: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.
cautions.renal: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.
cautions.hepatic: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.
cautions.cardiac: No specific interaction beyond general food-safety rules.
cautions.dysphagia: Combine texture modification from the mucositis/swallowing template as needed.
cautions.ostomy: Individualize with the ostomy team; food-safety rules still apply.
cautions.obstruction: Not applicable to food safety specifically.
cautions.immunosuppression: This is the primary trigger condition for the entire template.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: fever during known or suspected neutropenia (medical emergency, not a diet question)
any GI illness symptom during neutropenia/transplant/immunosuppression
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet

templates.goal: Support general long-term health once the patient is nutritionally stable and no longer in an acute symptom-management phase.
templates.intended_population: Adult cancer survivors who are nutritionally stable, per current guideline scope (ASCO exercise/diet/weight-management guideline).
may_apply_when: a current oncology guideline applies to the general survivorship population being addressed
unsuitable_when: patient is not nutritionally stable (use a symptom-specific template above instead)
the intended use is a cancer-type-specific diet claim -- no such diet is included in this proposal absent a guideline supporting that exact disease/treatment context
templates.flexible_food_pattern: General healthy-eating pattern consistent with current oncology survivorship guidance (adequate fruits/vegetables, whole grains, lean protein, limited processed/red meat and alcohol, weight management as clinically appropriate) -- not a rigid menu.
chinese_food_examples_and_substitutions: A variety of vegetables prepared by steaming, stir-frying with modest oil, or in soup
Soy foods (tofu, soy milk) as a lean protein option
Whole grains such as brown rice or whole-grain noodles as tolerated
Fish and poultry prepared with modest oil and seasoning
templates.traditional_dietary_therapy_context: General balance-and-moderation concepts in Chinese food culture (e.g. varied, seasonal, moderately portioned meals) may be mentioned as cultural framing for these food choices, kept separate from the guideline-based biomedical rationale below.
templates.biomedical_rationale: Per the ASCO guideline on exercise, diet, and weight management during cancer treatment/survivorship: general healthy-eating and weight-management patterns support long-term health; this is a general-health rationale, not a cancer-cure or recurrence-prevention claim for any specific food.
templates.protein_energy_fluid_texture_food_safety: No acute-phase food-safety restriction unless another concurrent condition (e.g. ongoing immunosuppression) applies; portion/energy guidance follows general healthy-eating principles, not an automatic individualized calculation.
templates.medication_herb_supplement_food_interact: This template does not add any herb, tea, or supplement; any survivor interest in a specific herb or supplement (e.g. green tea extract, ginseng) is routed to the herb/supplement evidence cards, never bundled into 'healthy eating.'

cautions.dysphagia: Not the primary population for this template; use an acute-symptom template if dysphagia is present.
cautions.obstruction: Not applicable to a stable survivorship population.
cautions.allergy: Screen all food examples for known allergy.
cautions.immunosuppression: If ongoing (e.g. late post-transplant), combine with the food-safety template.

red_flags_requiring_escalation: unintentional weight loss or new GI symptoms in a previously stable survivor -- re-refer to oncology dietitian
templates.expiry_review: review required within 12 months of approval date; no approval date set yet
